title: Reduction of the flat model
statement:
Let $A_{E,m}$ and $A_{E,n}$ be two finite coefficient stages with
$m\leq n$, let $T$ be a scheme on which $\ell$ is invertible, let
$K\in D^b_c(T,A_{E,n})$ be a bounded constructible complex of
$A_{E,n}$-modules on the small pro-étale site or on the small étale
site, and let $P\cong K$ be a bounded flat model of $K$ in degrees
$[a,b]$ in the sense of [lem-sf-flat-model]: each $P^q$ is a flat
$A_{E,n}$-module sheaf and $P^q=0$ for $q\notin[a,b]$. Write
$K_m=K\otimes^L_{A_{E,n}}A_{E,m}$ for the reduction of $K$. Then
$P\otimes_{A_{E,n}}A_{E,m}$ is a bounded flat model of $K_m$ in the
same interval:

$$
K_m\cong P\otimes_{A_{E,n}}A_{E,m},\qquad
(P\otimes_{A_{E,n}}A_{E,m})^q=0\quad(q\notin[a,b]),
$$

and each term $P^q\otimes_{A_{E,n}}A_{E,m}$ is a flat
$A_{E,m}$-module sheaf. Consequently the reduction $K_m$ has finite
Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ as soon
as $K$ does.

proof.text: Set R=(A_{E,n})_T and S=(A_{E,m})_T and use the canonical quotient factor map. The supplied upper support bound makes P strictly bounded above. Apply lem-weil-pbc-independent-bounded-flat-kflat to obtain K-flatness at the actual independent site universes. The chosen ordinary functor has the prescribed changeOfRings objects and maps, so lem-pur-kflat-change-of-rings-independent gives flat reduced terms. The site tensor comparison of lem-weil-pbc-independent-sheaf-tensor-colimits identifies this categorical flatness with IsFlatOnSite. Additivity sends every zero term outside [a,b] to zero.

The universal derived-change-of-rings counit is invertible on the K-flat P. Compose the image of K ≅ Q(P), the quotient-to-homotopy-localization comparison, that counit, and the target localization comparison. This gives Lφ*(K) ≅ Q(Pm) over S, with Pm the actual termwise ordinary scalar extension. The construction uses the universal pair already fixed in flatModelReductionDerivedData; no new choice of derived functor is made.

For the pro-etale Tor conclusion use the public comparison family in lem-sf-ringed-kflat-single-tensor-comparison. For any K-flat resolution P′→L of K_m, mapBifunctorSingle₂Iso identifies its native total tensor with its termwise tensor by the arbitrary test sheaf M. The public comparison identifies the latter with the published derived site tensor on Q(P′) and M[0]. Transport in its first argument along Q(P′) ≅ Q(L) ≅ K_m ≅ Q(Pm), then apply the comparison for the reduced K-flat model Pm. This yields an isomorphism with the termwise tensor of Pm by M. Every term outside [a,b] is zero because additive tensor preserves zero, so its homology vanishes there. Localization transports this vanishing to the arbitrary resolution in the original predicate. The original amplitude assumption supplies a≤b.

For the etale clause, compute the geometric stalk of the sheafified scalar extension as scalar extension of the original stalk. The geometric-stalk criterion and Module.Flat.baseChange show that every reduced term is flat over A_{E,m}; additivity preserves its support. Form the natural isomorphism F⋙Res ≅ tensorRight((A_{E,m})_T) using commutation of restriction with sheafification, ModuleCat.extendScalarsCompRestrictScalarsIso, the sectionwise constant-tensor comparison, and monoidal sheafification. Lift this isomorphism termwise to P, localize, and compose with derivedTensorQObjSingleFunctorObjIso and the image of K≅Q(P). This is exactly the required restricted derived-tensor comparison. Finally apply the generic bounded-flat Tor-amplitude theorem and hasTorAmplitudeIn_iff_torAmplitudeIn. This argument covers empty intervals too, since the support hypotheses then force P=0.
